_about: The one hand-written thing behind Higher or Lower. Every puzzle in
games/higher-or-lower/deck.js is DERIVED from this list by
tools/make-higher-or-lower.js - so a number corrected here corrects every
puzzle that uses it, and the bet and the guess about one number can never
Each number is asked two ways. As a BET, where another number from its
group is given first and the room says higher or lower. As a GUESS, with
three numbers to choose from. Both are variants of ONE puzzle, so a round
never asks about the same number twice.
Wrong options in a guess are always OTHER REAL NUMBERS from the same
group, never invented ones. An invented plausible number risks being a
real figure from somewhere else in the Bible, and a room told that 40 is
wrong deserves better than a number we made up.
_rule: The bar is not 'the number appears somewhere'. It is that the number is
STATED in the text - never summed or inferred - and reads the SAME in any
common translation. A confident wrong number on a screen in church is
worse than not having the game.

_excluded.why: the Masoretic 'six cubits and a span' against the Septuagint and Dead Sea Scrolls 'four cubits and a span'. Every common English Bible footnotes the other figure
KJV and NKJV read seventy times seven; NIV and ESV read seventy-seven times. A different number, not a different wording
manuscripts split between seventy and seventy-two
Exodus never says ten. The count is arrived at by tallying, and the rule is that the number must be stated
the text says six days and 'the seventh day'. Seven days is a sum. The seven circuits ON the last day ARE stated, and are used instead
the number is stable but translations split on whether it is her age or her years of widowhood, so no question can be asked unambiguously
conflicts with the 400 of Genesis 15:13, which is used instead. A sharp youth with an NIV may still raise it - the host should know

_excluded.what: 1 SAMUEL 6:19, THE CENSUS TOTALS, SOLOMON'S STALLS
_excluded.why: the parallel passages disagree with each other
arrived at by arithmetic, never stated

_collisions: Only one value per group, so a bet is always answerable. That cost some
famous numbers: keeping the 40 days of rain excluded Jesus' fast, Moses on
the mountain, the spies and Nineveh; keeping the 40 years of wandering
excluded David's and Solomon's reigns; keeping Jonah's three days excluded
Saul's blindness and Esther's fast. Any of them can be swapped in for the
